vulnerabilities.summary: A use-after-free in libxml2 can occur while parsing certain XPath elements in XML Schematron documents.
Processing certain sch:name elements in XML can trigger memory corruption in libxml2.

patches.title: Keep XPath namespace nodes alive during Schematron reporting
patches.description: Preserves the XPath result for the duration of Schematron report generation and checks node types before reading element fields.

tests.baselineExpectation: Valgrind identifies the Schematron invalid read on the vulnerable Focal binaries.
tests.patchedExpectation: The installed Focal backport completes both cases without invalid reads, and a normal xmllint consumer check passes.

vulnerabilities.summary: A crafted XML document can trigger a use-after-free while libxml2 handles parameter-entity input after parser error handling.

patches.title: Preserve parser input ownership during parameter-entity errors
patches.description: Backports the upstream input-ownership and parser EOF handling fixes to the pinned Debian libxml2 sources.

additionalCommits.purpose: Stop xmlSkipBlankChars at parser EOF during allocation-failure handling.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed Debian baseline reproduces the parameter-entity use-after-free under Valgrind.
tests.patchedExpectation: The exact installed patched package passes the same Valgrind regression with zero errors and passes the xmllint consumer check.

vulnerabilities.summary: A crafted XML document can trigger a use-after-free while libxml2 handles parameter-entity input after parser error handling.
XInclude processing ignored XML_PARSE_NONET and could trigger network access.
A malformed XML catalog nextCatalog entry without its required catalog attribute can crash libxml2.

patches.title: Preserve parameter entity input ownership at parser EOF
patches.description: Backports the parser-stop handling needed to avoid a heap use-after-free while parsing a crafted parameter-entity DTD.

additionalCommits.purpose: Stops xmlSkipBlankChars after parser EOF so allocation-failure handling cannot loop indefinitely.

tests.baselineExpectation: Exact-source ASan builds report a heap use-after-free; the installed-package runner must report a Valgrind invalid read in libxml2 during xmlReadMemory with the freed entity-stream allocation in the trace.
tests.patchedExpectation: The source-build ASan and installed-package Valgrind probes complete without invalid accesses; a normal xmllint consumer check passes.

patches.title: Propagate parser security flags through XInclude APIs
patches.description: Carries XML_PARSE_NONET from the parsed document into the public XInclude convenience APIs and text-include parser context, preventing a later XInclude pass from triggering a network load when parsing disabled network access.

tests.baselineExpectation: Against the exact installed Trixie baseline, both xmlXIncludeProcess and xmlXIncludeProcessTree make a harmless request to a loopback-only listener despite XML_PARSE_NONET.
tests.patchedExpectation: Against the exact installed GetPatched package, both APIs block the loopback request; no non-loopback network access is used.

patches.title: Ignore XML catalog nextCatalog entries without a catalog attribute
patches.description: Skips malformed nextCatalog entries before duplicate detection can dereference a missing catalog entry.

tests.baselineExpectation: On the exact installed Debian Trixie source baseline, Valgrind must identify the NULL dereference in libxml2 catalog duplicate detection when a valid nextCatalog is followed by one without the required catalog attribute.
tests.patchedExpectation: The installed patched package completes catalog loading and resolves the mapping from the valid nextCatalog with no Valgrind errors.

vulnerabilities.summary: A specially crafted RAR5 archive can make libarchive's decompression loop consume CPU without making forward progress.

patches.title: Reject RAR5 filter blocks larger than half the decoder window
patches.description: Rejects an oversized filter block before decoding can enter a state without forward progress.

tests.baselineExpectation: The vulnerable Focal archive probe times out on the bounded RAR5 fixture.
tests.patchedExpectation: The installed Focal backport rejects the fixture within the five-second limit; normal bsdtar create/extract checks pass.

patches.title: Allow two-byte Zstandard output variation in a tiny-input test
patches.description: Allows only the two-byte compression-size difference produced by Focal zstd while retaining the archive readback checks.

tests.baselineExpectation: The Focal zstd output size differs by two bytes from upstream's expected size.
tests.patchedExpectation: The size tolerance is limited to two bytes and archive readback assertions continue to run.

vulnerabilities.summary: A use-after-free in Poppler's StructTreeRoot parent-tree parser can be triggered by a crafted PDF.

patches.title: Reject duplicate parent-tree keys before vector resizing
patches.description: Backports the upstream guard that prevents stale Parent pointers after repeated keys trigger vector reallocation.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed baseline exits with Valgrind error code 97 and reports an invalid memory access in StructTreeRoot::parentTreeAdd.
tests.patchedExpectation: The exact installed patched package completes pdfinfo -struct with exit status 0 and Valgrind reports no errors.

vulnerabilities.summary: An overlong password in a revision 6 encrypted PDF can overflow fixed-size buffers in Poppler's password hashing code.

patches.title: Clamp overlong revision 6 PDF passwords before hashing
patches.description: Limits the revision 6 hash input to the PDF-specified 127 bytes so K1 and E remain within their fixed-size buffers.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed Debian baseline reproduces the long-password overflow under Valgrind in revision6Hash/Decrypt.cc, or the attributed stack-canary abort inside libpoppler.
tests.patchedExpectation: The exact installed patched package completes the same 180-byte owner-password probe with exit status 0 and Valgrind reports no errors.

vulnerabilities.summary: An overlong password in a revision 6 encrypted PDF can overflow fixed-size buffers in Poppler's password hashing code.

patches.title: Clamp overlong revision 6 PDF passwords before hashing
patches.description: Limits the revision 6 hash input to the PDF-specified 127 bytes so K1 and E remain within their fixed-size buffers.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed Debian baseline reproduces the long-password overflow under Valgrind in revision6Hash/Decrypt.cc, or the attributed stack-canary abort inside libpoppler.
tests.patchedExpectation: The exact installed patched package completes the same 180-byte owner-password probe with exit status 0 and Valgrind reports no errors.

vulnerabilities.summary: Malicious submodule paths can escape the repository worktree.
A malicious pack delta can declare an excessive object size and cause memory exhaustion.
An HTTP redirect can cause credentials for the original host to be exposed to another host.

patches.title: Reject submodule filesystem paths outside the repository
patches.description: Rejects traversal paths read from .gitmodules before submodule operations can escape the worktree.

tests.baselineExpectation: The installed baseline creates a malicious subrepository outside its worktree.
tests.patchedExpectation: The installed patched package rejects the path and creates no escaped directory.

patches.title: Bound declared object size while unpacking pack data
patches.description: Rejects an oversized declared delta result before allocating its memory.

tests.baselineExpectation: The installed baseline accepts a compact pack declaring a 100 MiB delta result.
tests.patchedExpectation: The installed patched package rejects the object at a configured 42 MiB cap.

patches.title: Pass redirected server URL to the credential callback
patches.description: Passes the actual redirected origin to the credential callback so credentials are not sent to an untrusted host.

tests.baselineExpectation: After redirect, the vulnerable callback receives the trusted origin and the redirected fixture server receives the dummy credential.
tests.patchedExpectation: After redirect, the callback receives the redirected origin and the fixture server receives no Authorization header.

vulnerabilities.summary: Malicious submodule paths can escape the repository worktree.
A malicious pack delta can declare an excessive object size and cause memory exhaustion.
An HTTP redirect can cause credentials for the original host to be exposed to another host.

patches.title: Reject submodule filesystem paths outside the repository
patches.description: Rejects traversal paths read from .gitmodules before submodule operations can escape the worktree.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed Jammy baseline resolves the malicious submodule path and creates the configured subrepository outside its worktree, inside an isolated temporary parent.
tests.patchedExpectation: The exact installed patched Jammy package rejects the path with GIT_EINVALID and creates no directory outside its worktree.

patches.title: Bound declared object size while unpacking pack data
patches.description: Rejects an oversized declared delta result before allocating its memory.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed Jammy baseline accepts the 150-byte pack carrying a declared 100 MiB delta result.
tests.patchedExpectation: The exact installed patched Jammy package rejects the object at a 42 MiB configured cap before allocating the declared result.

tests.baselineExpectation: Binary patch application succeeds with the default settings.
tests.patchedExpectation: A 16-byte binary patch succeeds while the pack object size cap is set to one byte.

patches.title: Pass redirected server URL to the credential callback
patches.description: Passes the actual redirected origin to the credential callback so credentials are not sent to an untrusted host.

tests.baselineExpectation: After redirecting to a second localhost origin, the vulnerable credential callback still receives the trusted original origin and returns a fixture-only Basic credential; the redirected server records that exact dummy credential.
tests.patchedExpectation: After redirecting to a second localhost origin, the patched callback receives the redirected origin, rejects it as untrusted, and the redirected server observes no Authorization header.

vulnerabilities.summary: c-ares CPU exhaustion from unbounded DNS compression-pointer chains

patches.title: Reject overlong DNS names after compression-pointer expansion
patches.description: Adds the RFC 1035 255-octet expanded wire-name bound to the legacy Focal c-ares 1.15 parser while retaining its existing pointer-hop cap.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact Focal 1.15.0 source accepts an expanded DNS wire name longer than 255 octets; a maximum-valid 255-octet name remains accepted.
tests.patchedExpectation: The installed parser rejects the same overlong name with ARES_EBADNAME and accepts the maximum-valid 255-octet name.

vulnerabilities.summary: c-ares CPU exhaustion from unbounded DNS compression-pointer chains

patches.title: Bound DNS name expansion and compression-pointer traversal
patches.description: Backports c-ares' parser limits for expanded DNS names and compression-pointer hops to the Trixie 1.34.5 source.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact Trixie source accepts the crafted 200-hop backward pointer chain and returns a parsed record.
tests.patchedExpectation: The parser returns ARES_EBADNAME and no record for the same bounded input; valid-name boundary compatibility tests pass.

vulnerabilities.summary: Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write on invalid block switches

patches.title: Reject invalid block switches before decoder state corruption
patches.description: Backports the upstream Brotli decoder fix so malformed block-switch input is returned as a permanent format error rather than accepted as a need for more input.

tests.baselineExpectation: The baseline oracle expects BROTLI_DECODER_RESULT_ERROR (0) with decoderError -9 (BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_LENGTH_1) after producing 16 MiB in 4,096 calls.
tests.patchedExpectation: The patched oracle expects decoderError -17 (BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH) within the 32 MiB/8,192-call hard bounds; normal compression round-trip must succeed.

vulnerabilities.summary: A high sample count can make tiffcrop's level-2 debug output exceed its fixed sample buffer.
An overflowing subdivision count can bypass tiffcrop’s section-count limit.
Certain PixarLog-compressed RGB TIFF strips can cause an out-of-bounds write in the 8BITABGR decoder.
A truncated 32-bit strip length can make tiff2pdf allocate too little memory for an oversized BigTIFF strip.

patches.title: Bound tiffcrop's debug sample dump loop
patches.description: Bounds the level-2 debug output loop to the MAX_SAMPLES capacity of its sample buffer.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed baseline reports its recorded Memcheck signature for the level-2 debug sample dump.
tests.patchedExpectation: The installed patched tiffcrop completes the same dump and tiffinfo reads the output.

patches.title: Reject tiffcrop subdivision counts that overflow unsigned arithmetic (Bookworm)
patches.description: Checks subdivision operands before multiplication in parsing, output-offset calculation, and section writing.

tests.baselineExpectation: tiffcrop -S 134217729:32 -h returns zero and displays usage on the exact installed baseline.
tests.patchedExpectation: The same bounded command returns nonzero and reports that the MAX_SECTIONS limit was exceeded.

patches.title: Bound PixarLog 8BITABGR output for RGB strips (Bookworm)
patches.description: Corrects the ABGR output cursor and bounds multi-row decoding against the caller's buffer size.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed Bookworm baseline reaches the PixarLog decoder and Memcheck reports invalid writes beyond the 24,576-byte caller buffer.
tests.patchedExpectation: The patched installed package rejects the undersized output buffer, returns nonzero from the decoder, and has zero Memcheck errors.

patches.title: Preserve 64-bit BigTIFF strip lengths in tiff2pdf (Bookworm)
patches.description: Keep StripByteCounts values above 32 bits intact when sizing the tiff2pdf strip buffer.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed baseline truncates the oversized strip length; Memcheck ties an invalid read to tiff2pdf and the undersized allocation.
tests.patchedExpectation: The patched installed package rejects the oversized allocation before the strip read and reports no Memcheck errors.

An overflowing subdivision count can bypass tiffcrop’s section-count limit.

tests.patchedExpectation: The installed patched tiffcrop completes the same dump and tiffinfo reads the output.

patches.title: Reject tiffcrop subdivision counts that overflow unsigned arithmetic (Trixie)
patches.description: Checks subdivision operands before multiplication in parsing, output-offset calculation, and section writing.

tests.baselineExpectation: tiffcrop -S 134217729:32 -h returns zero and displays usage on the exact installed baseline.

vulnerabilities.summary: An external-entity subparser can crash when it receives empty non-final input before document data.

patches.title: Handle empty non-final input in external-entity subparsers
patches.description: Handles XML_TOK_NONE during subparser initialization so later input is parsed without dereferencing an unset event pointer.

tests.baselineExpectation: The exact installed baseline crashes with SIGSEGV when an external-entity callback parses an empty non-final subparser chunk and resumes with a processing instruction.
tests.patchedExpectation: The exact installed patched package completes the same parse and invokes the processing-instruction handler once; xmlwf -v reports the matching patched Expat version.
